title: Credibility Assessment of Explicit Finite Element Models for Total Knee Replacement Wear and Contact Mechanics under NASA-STD-7009A
device: Cemented posterior-stabilized total knee replacement with modular UHMWPE tibial insert and CoCrMo femoral component

models.name: Explicit Full-Assembly Knee Model (EFA‑Knee)
models.what_it_computes: Transient tibiofemoral and patellofemoral contact pressure, shear traction, sliding distance, Archard-type cumulative wear depth, post–cam contact impulse, and insert–tray micromotion in a full implant construct with simplified soft-tissue constraints.

models.name: Explicit Contact Submodel (ECS‑Insert)
models.what_it_computes: High-resolution local contact mechanics of the polyethylene insert against the femoral component, including edge-loading, roughness-dependent frictional work density, wear increment, and interface-relative motion at the underside support using reduced boundary representations.

mechanisms.name: Tibiofemoral surface wear during level gait
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Long-term polyethylene volume loss and wear scar evolution relate to debris generation and survivorship.

mechanisms.name: Edge-loading under varus–valgus malalignment
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Malcontact elevates peak pressures and shear, accelerating local damage and potential insert rim distress.

mechanisms.name: Post–cam engagement impulse in deep flexion
mechanisms.why_it_matters: High-rate contact between the femoral cam and tibial post can drive local stress concentrations and fatigue onset.

mechanisms.name: Backside micromotion-induced fretting at insert–tray
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Relative motion at the modular interface contributes to backside wear and particulate generation.

deviation.detail: All factor scores for each model×mechanism pair are reported on a 0–7 Engineering Credibility Index (ECI) with an adequacy threshold of ECI≥5.
